raw_response:
A is ill-posed as a bridge test.
You can compute Window6’s own spectral order, but it will not non-circularly connect back to the bio  $E_1$  result.
The clean Window6 object would be:

$$X_6=\{x\in\{0,1\}^6:\text{no adjacent 1s}\},\quad |X_6|=21,$$

with centered indicator

$$f_W=\mathbf{1}_{X_6}-21/64$$

on the Boolean cube  $Q_6$ . Its natural spectral decomposition is Boolean Fourier degree:

$$f_W=\sum_{S\subseteq[6]}\hat f(S)\chi_S,$$

with degree energies

$$\rho_k(W)=
\frac{\sum_{|S|=k}\hat f(S)^2}
{\sum_{S\neq\varnothing}\hat f(S)^2}.$$

That is a valid pure-math diagnostic of Window6: is the no-adjacent-1 constraint mostly first-order, pairwise, or higher-order as a Boolean subset? A reasonable null would be all  $21$ -vertex subsets of  $Q_6$  matched for internal edge count  $38$ , and preferably also matched for coordinate-marginal multiset. Certification would mean Window6 has an extreme Boolean degree profile under that null.
But that would certify only a property of Window6. It would not bridge to the codon  $E_1$ .
The reason is fundamental: codon  $E_1$  is the first Krawtchouk layer of

$$H(3,4)=V_4^3,$$

so it means additive dependence on one codon position, with each position carrying the chemical  $V_4$  characters. Window6 Fourier degree 1 means additive dependence on one Boolean bit in  $Q_6$ . These are not the same coordinate system, not the same association scheme, and not the same biological object.
To compare them, you would need to group the six Window6 bits into three pairs to imitate  $V_4^3$ . But no such grouping is forced by Window6. Choosing one creates exactly the convention-dependence that the previous non-q6 embedding failures were meant to rule out. If you test all  $15$  pairings of six bits into three unordered pairs, then either the result is pairing-dependent, which is circular, or pairing-invariant, in which case it is a generic property of the Window6 language rather than a codon bridge.
So the only admissible Window6 spectral calculation is a negative-control audit, not a new bridge direction:


If Window6 is high-order while bio is  $E_1$ , that supports an inverse analogy rhetorically, but not a forcing result.


If Window6 is first-order too, that still does not imply alignment, because the first-order frames are not identified.


If alignment appears only after selecting a special bit-pairing, it is convention-circular.


If no alignment appears, it simply confirms that the spectral bridge is closed.


The bio  $E_1$  result is therefore best interpreted plainly: the B $^*_{Q6}$  residual is a codon-intrinsic single-position base-chemistry signal, localized to wobble, position 1, weak/strong, and purine/pyrimidine. That is biologically plausible and structurally clean, but it is not a Window6/Fibonacci signature. It says the residual lives in ordinary additive codon chemistry, not in the hoped-for  $\lambda=-3$  high-frequency layer.
So the honest answer to B is:
the bridge is correctly bio-gated; the decisive next input is the expanded organism set for the held-out cross-organism gate.
There is no remaining pure-math/public-data step that can non-vacuously connect the certified codon- $E_1$  residual back to Window6 without importing a non-canonical coordinate map. The structural program is genuinely exhausted, except for documenting Window6’s own Fourier degree profile as a negative control.
The sharpest next question is: In a larger held-out organism panel, does the certified codon- $E_1$  wobble/position-1 residual remain reproducible after tRNA-tAI, TE, clade, and composition controls, or is it only a codon-spelling artifact?
